name: Plate Loaded Lat Pulldown
grip: Semi-neutral or underhand grip on machine lever handles.
description: Pull bilateral converging plate-loaded lever arms downward to the upper chest while seated with thighs secured under roller pads.
setup: Load weight plates evenly onto both machine lever horns.
Adjust the thigh pads so your legs are firmly secured with feet flat on the floor.
Sit tall, grasp the overhead lever handles, and allow arms to fully extend overhead into a deep lat stretch.
instructions: Pull both lever arms downward and slightly inward toward your upper chest along the converging arc.
Drive your elbows down and back tight toward your ribcage.
Pause briefly at peak contraction with chest lifted and lats fully engaged.
Control the ascent slowly until your arms are fully extended overhead before initiating the next repetition.
cues: Drive elbows down to the ribs.
commonMistakes: Leaning excessively backward to swing the weight down.
Letting the levers crash into the top stops between reps.
Lifting thighs off the support pads.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates loaded (one per lever): record 40 kg total plate load.
logging.note: Plate-loaded machines feature converging lever arcs; record the total mass of plates loaded across both horns.

variantNote: Bilateral vertical pull on a converging plate-loaded machine with dual lever arms.
